credit_metrics.text: EBITDA rose by {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda@FY2024}}, lifting the EBITDA margin by {{ebitda_margin.change@FY2024}} to {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}}.
Gross leverage fell by {{gross_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{gross_leverage@FY2024}}, with net debt reduced by {{net_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{net_debt@FY2024}}.
Cash generation strengthened: FFO rose by {{ffo.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo@FY2024}} and FFO to debt by {{ffo_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{ffo_to_debt@FY2024}}.

Free cash flow rose by {{fcf.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf@FY2024}}, taking FCF to debt up by {{fcf_to_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{fcf_to_debt@FY2024}} as capex intensity eased by {{capex_intensity.change@FY2024}} to {{capex_intensity@FY2024}}.
Interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, still a comfortable level against the peer median.

liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments fell by {{cash_like.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_like@FY2024}}, and cash liquidity by the same measure to {{cash_liquidity@FY2024}}.
In FY2023 the group held liquidity of {{liquidity@FY2023}}, including {{undrawn_facilities@FY2023}} of undrawn committed facilities, and liquidity to revenue of {{liquidity_to_revenue@FY2023}}.

The cash decline reflects debt repayment, with total debt down {{total_debt.change@FY2024}} to {{total_debt@FY2024}}, and the rating actions in the year left the group at investment grade with a stable outlook at Fitch.

operating_performance.text: Passengers rose by {{passengers.change@FY2024}} to {{passengers@FY2024}}, though traffic growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2024}}.

Aeronautical revenue per passenger rose by {{aero_revenue_per_passenger.change@FY2024}} to {{aero_revenue_per_passenger@FY2024}}, with the CNMC setting the 2025 maximum adjusted revenue per passenger unchanged on the prior year.

Operating profit rose by {{operating_profit.change@FY2024}} to {{operating_profit@FY2024}}, and profit for the year by {{profit.change@FY2024}} to {{profit@FY2024}}, the latter including the gain on the sale of the ESSP SAS stake.

peer_positioning.text: Aena has the highest EBITDA margin in the airport group ({{ebitda_margin.peer_rank@2024}}), at {{ebitda_margin@FY2024}} against a peer median of {{ebitda_margin.peer_median@2024}}.
Gross leverage of {{gross_leverage@FY2024}} puts the company in the middle of the group ({{gross_leverage.peer_rank@2024}}).
It leads the group on interest coverage ({{interest_coverage.peer_rank@2024}}), FFO to debt ({{ffo_to_debt.peer_rank@2024}}) and FCF to debt ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@2024}}).

Traffic growth of {{traffic_growth@FY2024}} is above the peer median of {{traffic_growth.peer_median@2024}} and ranks {{traffic_growth.peer_rank@2024}}, while capex intensity of {{capex_intensity@FY2024}} is below the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@2024}}.

snapshot.text: Aena, the Spanish airport operator, grew revenue by {{revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{revenue@FY2024}} in FY2024, and both Fitch and Moody's moved its ratings or outlook in the year.
Net leverage fell by {{net_leverage.change@FY2024}} to {{net_leverage@FY2024}}, helped by EBITDA up {{ebitda.change@FY2024}} and total debt down {{total_debt.change@FY2024}}.
The point to watch is liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}} as cash was used to repay debt.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2024}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2024}}, so the buffer against maturities is thinner than a year earlier.

Coverage: interest coverage eased by {{interest_coverage.change@FY2024}} to {{interest_coverage@FY2024}}, a mild weakening even though it remains above the peer median of {{interest_coverage.peer_median@2024}}.
Traffic: growth slowed by {{traffic_growth.change@FY2024}} to {{traffic_growth@FY2024}}, which matters because the CNMC left the 2025 maximum adjusted revenue per passenger unchanged.
Portfolio: the Cartagena concession ended in the year, so the contribution from the Latin American operations is smaller.
